places._note: WO-162 Part 5: a ruling on a place replaces that field of the place in the index, keyed by the place's name. The generated file is never edited by hand.

Castle Volkihar._why: Quest words call it Volkihar Keep; its page is Castle Volkihar. WO-178 Part 2: the records name no hold for it; it stands on an island off Haafingar's coast, and Solitude, Haafingar's capital, is its nearest city.
Castle Volkihar._posWhy: WO-178 Part 3: the game's own marker (and the island's doors, 170,000 to 176,000 units west, 148,000 to 154,000 north) put the castle at (-177219, 147389), 28,000 units west of where the paper map draws its island, so the pin fell in open sea. The pin is moved onto the drawn island (the crescent northwest of Haafingar's coast); the game's own position stays in places_raw.json.

Dimhollow Crypt._why: Quest words call it Dimhollow Cavern; its page is Dimhollow Crypt.

Driftshade Sanctuary._why: Quest words call it Driftshade Refuge; its page is Driftshade Sanctuary.

High Hrothgar._why: The records type High Hrothgar a Fort, with trolls on the path up. It is the Greybeards' home, where people live, so it gets the lived-in page. WO-178: it is nearest Riverwood in a straight line (0.4 km), but no player walks that way; the only road up is the 7,000 Steps from Ivarstead (0.5 km on the map, a climb of 11,750 units), so Ivarstead is its town and `gettingThere` says the way.

Bleak Falls Barrow._why: A ruin on the mountain above Riverwood: 0.3 km on the flat map and 5,866 units up the path, so "next to it" is wrong and it is a climb. Only a place marked `mountain` is said to be up one; height alone is not enough (Riverwood is 'above' Whiterun, Blackreach is under everything).

Soul Cairn._why: Another plane, with no position on Tamriel's map: what it is and how you get there.
Soul Cairn.gettingThere: Through the portal in Castle Volkihar

people._note: WO-159: a fact a player found in game replaces the read's field for that person, the way questStarts does for a quest start. The build marks the replaced fields as from players, drops the read's doubts about them, and counts one approved report. Keyed by the person's name.

Alvor._why: The records give Alvor no job keyword; he is the smith in Riverwood, so a place page can say what he sells.

Jaree-Ra._source: Dave, watched in game for a day, 23 Oct 2026
Jaree-Ra._why: The reads put Jaree-Ra on the Solitude docks and the Red Wave. Dave watched him for a full in-game day: he stands in Solitude by the Winking Skeever, day and night, and never goes to the docks or the Red Wave (WO-152 Part 0).
Jaree-Ra.firstMeet: In Solitude, by the Winking Skeever.

day.doing: standing about; he stays there day and night

changes: Lights Out! settles what happens to him: he can be arrested if you report him, killed on the docks, persuaded to give up, or followed to Broken Oar Grotto with the stolen loot and killed there; he can also become your partner in looting the Icerunner.

questAliases._note: WO-180 Part 7a (Bob, 30 Oct): a story quest always has its person; the records leave some of them as an alias filled at run time (a courier spawned at a marker, an authority figure found by condition, a copy of the follower alias). plain_alias would say 'the person the job names' for them. These say them as the quest's read does, by editor id (a trailing * is a prefix) and alias name: {edid: {alias: words}}.
